newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Landmarks focuses on hospital management.
newsitem.headline: Landmarks focuses on hospital management.

text.p: Malaysian hotel property developer Landmarks Bhd said on Friday it planned to increase its exposure to the hospital management industry, the national Bernama news agency reported.
The company intends to invest around 200 million ringgit in setting up two private hospitals near Kuala Lumpur before 2000, said Bernama.
The move would involve the selling of its stake in hotel group Shangri-La (Malaysia) Bhd, said Landmarks managing director Mohamed Abdul Halim Ahmad.
No buyers had been identified but eventually Landmarks might transfer its other hotel holdings to another company, said Abdul Halim.
Abdul Halim said the group foresaw ample opportunity in the healthcare industry in Malaysia and intended to participate in the country's healthcare privatisation programme.
Landmarks was looking through its portfolio to either sell or list some of its properties, said Abdul Halim.

"There may be a possible listing of Sungai Wang Plaza (a Kuala Lumpur shopping mall) but it is still in the midst of discussion. However, priority may not be given to Sungai Wang alone as we will be doing it in a package," Abdul Halim was quoted as saying.
In January, Landmarks said it proposed to acquire an indirect stake in Australian Hospital Care Ltd. The company operates 13 hospitals, most in the Melbourne area.
